obligations.text: repo -o -name R -trust-server URL sets the trust server of one ORAS repository, and an empty value removes it.
obligations.cases: set, clear, absent
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: The trust server URL must use https and is stored in canonical form.
obligations.cases: https valid, http, other scheme, invalid
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: A refused value changes nothing, including the default deployment flag -publish 1 would have moved.
obligations.cases: refusal with and without -publish 1
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: repo -list, repo -copy-from and lock files keep the trust server; a stored value that is not https fails every check.
obligations.cases: package service, publish service, copy, lock entry; stored http value
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)
obligations.gap: Carrying the value is transcribed as identity functions (rule 4a); %ConstructClone, the JSON lock mapping and repo -list display are native-tested (TestRepoConfiguration), not modeled.

obligations.text: Other repository types refuse -trust-server without being created or changed.
obligations.cases: ORAS vs remote vs filesystem
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: config set NotaryExecutable names the verifier; config delete NotaryExecutable returns to notary on the PATH.
obligations.cases: set first/last path, delete
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: A tag is accepted as docker pull accepts it: signed in targets/releases, or else in targets.
obligations.cases: releases, targets, other role, first row per tag
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: notary reaches the trust server over TLS and checks its certificate, so the first check pins the root an authenticated trust server presents; later trust data chains to it.
obligations.cases: https vs http, pinned vs first use, presented vs authentic root
obligations.observation: root a listing was accepted under
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems); premises tls_authenticated, notary_verified, pins_authentic

obligations.text: Pins are kept per trust server under the IRIS manager directory, so every namespace of the instance uses the same pins.
obligations.cases: two namespaces, two trust servers
obligations.basis: native: TestVerifierUnavailableRefused reads TrustDirectory; the directory key and namespace sharing are not modeled
obligations.gap: No formal rule distinguishes the pin directory per trust server or its sharing across namespaces.

obligations.text: A signature only in another delegation role does not count.
obligations.cases: targets/other only
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: Each check must reach the trust server; an unreachable server, a verifier that cannot run or failed verification refuses instead of using cached trust data.
obligations.cases: reachable, unreachable with valid cached data, verifier missing
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: Each check runs notary in its own trust directory seeded with the pins but no timestamp, so no other check can supply one.
obligations.cases: every interleaving of checks of one repository, shared vs private directory
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: Checks of one repository on one trust server run one at a time, only a successful check replaces the pins, and the pins never include a timestamp.
obligations.cases: locked vs unlocked, accepted vs refused finish
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)
obligations.gap: The pin store itself is abstracted to its root version; that it never holds timestamp.json is represented by seeding never carrying one (control timestamp-seeded), not by a modeled pin file set.

obligations.text: A server with no trust data for the repository means nothing in it is signed.
obligations.cases: NoTrustData
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: A check that does not finish in time fails, and the repo's other checks on that trust server fail at once for the rest of the command.
obligations.cases: timeout, later repository on same server, other server
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: The signed manifest and its package are downloaded by digest and their size and digest checked before anything unpacks them.
obligations.cases: matching, wrong digest, wrong size for manifest and package

obligations.text: One check of size and digest serves both the manifest and the package.
obligations.cases: digest-only and size-only checks
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: The signed manifest must have exactly one package layer.
obligations.cases: zero, one, two package layers
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)

obligations.text: Other layers are never downloaded or unpacked.
obligations.cases: manifest with a directory layer
obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems)
obligations.gap: provider_unpacked is a transcribed constant (rule 4a); native TestNothingUnpackedBeforeVerification distinguishes it against the unprotected pull.

obligations.text: A failed check deletes the download and leaves the installed module as it was.

obligations.gap: Deleting the download is not modeled; native TestNothingUnpackedBeforeVerification and TestWrongBytesRefused observe it.

obligations.text: A refused check fails the command, history records it as failed, the rejected lifecycle does not run, and an installed version stays usable.

obligations.basis: new:issue281-d3 (Verus, 32 controls rejected at named theorems); coverage iter74 replayed
obligations.gap: Installed code staying usable is observed natively (AssertRevision), not modeled.

obligations.text: -force, -dev and the other install options do not skip the check.
